doc.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023

title: Meat Loaf session and a written solo
summary: Marini recalls a Meat Loaf session where the producer had written out the solo.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Nice. What about, same year, Meat Loaf.

Yeah. You know I remember that too. It’s funny that you picked that one because Meat Loaf, that music, it’s like Bruce Springsteen to me. Clarence Clemmons could play a great solo at the drop of a hat. That stuff for me, I have so much difficulty trying to play a solo over that kind of stuff. And I remember that session because at the end of the session the producer said, “Lou, don’t pack up yet, I want you to play a solo on this one tune.” And my heart sank you know. I’m thinking oh fuck. So — those driving — and then he said, “I hope you don’t mind but I had an idea for this solo so I wrote one out.” I was like, “No, no, I don’t mind at all.” So that was a written solo, not by me. I may have modified it in the playing of it but yeah, I remember that.
